_why: Each entry binds a parity oracle to the c43 file whose behaviour it reproduces. `frozen` oracles are hand-transliterated and CANNOT see c43 move, so they are gated on a content hash of what they mirror; the endpoint is an empty list, not a maintained one. `generated` oracles are extracted from c43 source and are sound in shape -- they are gated on reproducing byte-identically, because nothing else re-runs the extractor.
_converted: ALL FIVE ARE CONVERTED. flags_oracle.c, program_serialization_oracle.c, calc_state_oracle.c, register_metadata_oracle.c and keyboard_state_oracle.c have all left this list: each now #includes its c43 counterpart under oracle_* names, so the reference moves with c43 by construction and there is nothing left to hash. The last three took the FULL-CORE shape (build/host/steps.zig) rather than a linked unit oracle, because sharing the value codecs, the register subsystem and the keyboard's GTK-bound entry path for real needs the whole calculator; the payoff is that those lanes compare .sav BYTES, the RAM slab itself, and the state a keystroke leaves behind. Entries leave here by being converted, never by being excused, and the list is meant to stay empty.

generated.why: Extracted from src/c47/charString.c by its own script, so the reference moves with c43 -- but the script's header comment claimed 'the harness fails if the committed oracle is stale' and nothing in the tree re-ran it. Sound shape, ungated until now.
